children.title: Stochastic Convex Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Organizes noise-limited convex complexity across smooth and nonsmooth classes.

children.title: Nonsmooth Stochastic Convex Regime
children.top_down_role: Navigation for Lipschitz stochastic objectives and subgradient information.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth Stochastic Convex Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimax stochastic first-order lower bound for Lipschitz convex objectives on a bounded domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) be convex with Euclidean radius at least \(R\), and consider convex \(G\)-Lipschitz objectives \(F\) on \(X\). A stochastic first-order oracle returns \(g(x,\xi)\) satisfying \(\mathbb E[g(x,\xi)]\in\partial F(x)\) and \(\mathbb E\lVert g(x,\xi)\rVert^2\leq G^2\). For every algorithm using at most \(T\) adaptive oracle calls, in sufficiently large dimension there exists an admissible instance such that \[\mathbb E[F(\widehat x_T)-\min_{x\in X}F(x)]\geq c\frac{GR}{\sqrt T},\] where \(c>0\) is universal. Thus expected error \(\varepsilon\) requires \(T=\Omega(G^2R^2/\varepsilon^2)\) calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonsmooth Lipschitz stochastic convex optimization, worst-case expected error cannot decay faster than order GR divided by the square root of queries.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is convex and \(G\)-Lipschitz on a convex domain of radius at least \(R\).
The stochastic subgradient oracle is unbiased and has second moment at most \(G^2\).
The ambient dimension is sufficiently large relative to \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{\mathcal A}\sup_F\mathbb E[F(\widehat x_T)-F^*]=\Omega(GR/\sqrt T)\), hence \(T=\Omega(G^2R^2/\varepsilon^2)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the regime, and the rate is a standard candidate form, but no cited theorem fixes the admissible domain geometry, oracle distribution, output model, dimension requirement, or universal constants. Those details materially determine the valid minimax statement.

children.title: Smooth Stochastic Convex Regime
children.top_down_role: Navigation for deterministic transients and noise-dominated complexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Stochastic Convex Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined deterministic-transient and stochastic-noise lower bound for smooth convex minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) contain a Euclidean ball of radius \(R\), and let \(F\) be convex with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient. Suppose a stochastic gradient oracle returns \(g(x,\xi)\) with \(\mathbb E[g(x,\xi)]=\nabla F(x)\) and \(\mathbb E\lVert g(x,\xi)-\nabla F(x)\rVert^2\leq\sigma^2\). For every method using \(T\) adaptive calls, sufficiently large-dimensional instances satisfy \[\mathbb E[F(\widehat x_T)-F^*]\geq c\left(\frac{LR^2}{T^2}+\frac{\sigma R}{\sqrt T}\right)\] up to universal constant-factor equivalence. Consequently, accuracy \(\varepsilon\) requires \(T=\Omega(\sqrt{LR^2/\varepsilon}+\sigma^2R^2/\varepsilon^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smooth stochastic convex complexity combines an accelerated deterministic transient with a slower noise-dominated statistical term.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is convex with an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
The oracle is unbiased with variance at most \(\sigma^2\).
The feasible radius is at least \(R\), and dimension is sufficiently large.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimax expected error is \(\Omega(LR^2/T^2+\sigma R/\sqrt T)\) up to universal constants.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated deterministic and stochastic terms are plausible, but a source is required to establish that they hold simultaneously for the same oracle class and instance family, and to determine whether the theorem is naturally stated as a sum or maximum. The exact radius, dimension, and output assumptions are also unresolved.

children.title: Strongly Convex Stochastic Regime
children.top_down_role: Navigation for curvature-assisted stochastic complexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Stochastic Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noise-dominated minimax lower bound under strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex and let a stochastic first-order oracle return \(g(x,\xi)\) satisfying \(\mathbb E[g(x,\xi)]=\nabla F(x)\) and \(\mathbb E\lVert g(x,\xi)-\nabla F(x)\rVert^2\leq\sigma^2\). For every algorithm based on \(T\) adaptive oracle calls, an admissible instance exists for which \[\mathbb E[F(\widehat x_T)-F^*]\geq c\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu T},\] with a universal constant \(c>0\), under the theorem's required dimension and initialization conditions. Hence expected objective accuracy \(\varepsilon\) requires \(T=\Omega(\sigma^2/(\mu\varepsilon))\) stochastic first-order calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity improves the noise-dominated stochastic lower bound to order sigma squared divided by mu times the query count.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex.
The stochastic gradient is unbiased with variance at most \(\sigma^2\).
The dimension and initial domain satisfy the lower-bound construction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{\mathcal A}\sup_F\mathbb E[F(\widehat x_T)-F^*]=\Omega(\sigma^2/(\mu T))\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The noise-dominated rate is a standard candidate, but the record defers essential dimension and initialization hypotheses to an unnamed theorem. A source must specify the differentiability or smoothness class, oracle model, parameter range, and conditions under which the objective-error lower bound holds.

children.title: Optimization-Estimation Information Boundary
children.top_down_role: Navigation for the boundary between iterative optimization error and statistical information limits.

children.title: Iterative Optimization Limit
children.top_down_role: Error attributable to finite optimization progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterative Optimization Limit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic first-order obstruction forming the optimization component of a stochastic lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider convex functions \(F\) with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and an optimizer \(x^*\) satisfying \(\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert\leq R\). Even when stochastic noise vanishes, any method using \(T\) adaptive first-order queries has, in sufficiently large dimension, a worst-case instance satisfying \[F(\widehat x_T)-F^*\geq c\frac{LR^2}{(T+1)^2},\] where \(c>0\) is universal. Therefore a stochastic method cannot remove this iterative optimization transient merely by increasing sample quality; attaining objective error \(\varepsilon\) requires at least \(T=\Omega(\sqrt{LR^2/\varepsilon})\) sequential first-order rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Before noise dominates, smooth convex optimization retains the deterministic lower bound proportional to LR squared over the square of iteration count.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is convex with an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
An optimizer obeys \(\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert\leq R\).
Dimension is sufficiently large for the resisting-oracle construction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(\widehat x_T)-F^*=\Omega(LR^2/(T+1)^2)\), so \(T=\Omega(\sqrt{LR^2/\varepsilon})\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deterministic smooth-convex obstruction fits the terminal container, but no cited lower-bound theorem supports the quantified claim. A source is needed to distinguish deterministic from randomized algorithms and to state the resisting-oracle dimension and admissible output assumptions.

children.title: Statistical Estimation Limit
children.top_down_role: Error imposed by finite noisy information.

knowledge_statements.title: Statistical Estimation Limit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noise-induced estimation obstruction within stochastic convex optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let convex objectives be defined on a set containing points at distance scale \(R\), and let an unbiased stochastic first-order oracle have variance at most \(\sigma^2\). For every estimator \(\widehat x_T\) constructed from \(T\) oracle samples, a sufficiently rich admissible family contains an instance satisfying \[\mathbb E[F(\widehat x_T)-F^*]\geq c\frac{\sigma R}{\sqrt T},\] where \(c>0\) is universal. This lower bound persists independently of deterministic acceleration because it arises from distinguishing noisy instances. Consequently, expected objective accuracy \(\varepsilon\) requires at least \(T=\Omega(\sigma^2R^2/\varepsilon^2)\) statistically informative samples.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noisy oracle observations impose an estimation error of order sigma times radius over the square root of the number of samples.
assumptions_latex: The objective family is convex and has geometric scale \(R\).
Oracle observations are unbiased with variance at most \(\sigma^2\).
The admissible family contains the required indistinguishable-instance construction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{\widehat x_T}\sup_F\mathbb E[F(\widehat x_T)-F^*]=\Omega(\sigma R/\sqrt T)\).

notation.meaning: Output based on T stochastic observations.
Geometric scale of the instance family.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statistical-estimation interpretation fits the terminal container, but the objective family, geometry, and indistinguishable-instance construction are placeholders rather than explicit hypotheses. A source is required to determine the precise oracle and family for which the stated minimax lower bound is valid.

children.title: Optimization–Estimation Transition
children.top_down_role: Regimes where the dominant lower-bound mechanism changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimization–Estimation Transition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Crossover for Lipschitz stochastic convex population-risk minimization with finite samples and oracle queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be a worst-case class of convex \(L\)-Lipschitz losses on a convex set of radius \(R\). Suppose an algorithm observes at most \(n\) independent samples and makes at most \(T\) unbiased stochastic first-order queries, each revealing information from one observed loss. For universal constants \(c,C>0\), the characteristic minimax excess-risk scale is \[cLR\max\{n^{-1/2},T^{-1/2}\}\leq \mathcal E_{n,T}\leq CLR\bigl(n^{-1/2}+T^{-1/2}\bigr).\] Thus optimization error dominates when \(T<n\), statistical estimation error dominates when \(T>n\), and the transition occurs at \(T\asymp n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Worst-case excess risk changes from query-limited to sample-limited near the point where the number of stochastic oracle calls equals the number of independent samples.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\) consists of convex \(L\)-Lipschitz losses on a domain of radius \(R\).
The oracle is unbiased and exposes information from no more than \(n\) independent observations.
Performance is worst-case expected excess population risk after at most \(T\) queries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal E_{n,T}=\Theta\!\left(LR\max\{n^{-1/2},T^{-1/2}\}\right)\) up to universal constant-factor equivalence between maximum and sum formulations.

notation.meaning: minimax expected excess population risk with n samples and T queries
sample budget and stochastic first-order query budget

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The terminal kind and crossover interpretation fit the container, but the asserted two-budget minimax lower and upper bounds depend critically on the sample-reuse and oracle-information model. No source or locator supports the exact formula, universal constants, or matching hypotheses.

children.title: Sample–Query Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Comparisons between information acquisition and iterative oracle use.

knowledge_statements.title: Sample–Query Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effective-information lower bound when both independent samples and stochastic first-order queries are limited.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For convex \(L\)-Lipschitz stochastic losses on a domain of radius \(R\), consider algorithms using at most \(n\) independent samples and \(T\) stochastic first-order oracle calls. If a call cannot reveal an independent observation beyond the available sample budget, then the effective independent-information budget is \(m=\min\{n,T\}\). There is a universal constant \(c>0\) and, for every such algorithm, an admissible problem instance satisfying \[\mathbb E[F(\widehat x)-\inf_x F(x)]\geq cLRm^{-1/2}=cLR\max\{n^{-1/2},T^{-1/2}\}.\] Increasing only the larger budget cannot improve this lower-bound scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The smaller of the independent-sample and oracle-query budgets controls the worst-case information bound; enlarging only the larger budget cannot change the square-root rate.
assumptions_latex: The loss is convex and \(L\)-Lipschitz on a convex domain of radius \(R\).
At most \(n\) independent observations and \(T\) first-order oracle responses are available.
Each response contains information from at most one available observation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[F(\widehat x)-\inf_xF(x)]\geq cLR/\sqrt{\min\{n,T\}}\) on some admissible instance.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits Sample–Query Tradeoff, but identifying the effective information budget with min(n,T) is model-dependent, especially when samples can be revisited or a query can reveal more than one scalar observation. An authoritative lower-bound source with an exact oracle model and locator is required.

children.title: Stochastic Oracle Noise Classes
children.top_down_role: Separates lower bounds according to permissible noise and sampling behavior.

children.title: Concentrated Stochastic Noise Classes
children.top_down_role: Navigation for classical unbiased stochastic-oracle models.

children.title: Bounded-Variance Oracle Model
children.top_down_role: Stochastic lower bounds under finite uniform variance control.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Variance Oracle Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional second-moment model for an unbiased stochastic first-order oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable on \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), and let \(G(x,\zeta)\) be a stochastic first-order oracle. The oracle has uniformly bounded variance \(\sigma^2\) if, for every query \(x\in\mathcal X\), \[\mathbb E[G(x,\zeta)\mid x]=\nabla f(x),\qquad \mathbb E[\|G(x,\zeta)-\nabla f(x)\|_*^2\mid x]\leq\sigma^2.\] For adaptive queries, these conditions are interpreted conditionally on the history preceding the query. The bound controls the centered oracle noise rather than the second moment of the full stochastic gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbiased stochastic gradient oracle has bounded variance when its centered error has a uniformly bounded conditional second moment at every query point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable on \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\).
The query point may be random but is measurable with respect to the preceding history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[G(x,\zeta)\mid x]=\nabla f(x)\) and \(\mathbb E[\|G(x,\zeta)-\nabla f(x)\|_*^2\mid x]\leq\sigma^2\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).

children.title: Sub-Gaussian Noise Regime
children.top_down_role: Complexity under strong tail concentration.

knowledge_statements.title: Sub-Gaussian Noise Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional directional sub-Gaussian condition for centered stochastic-oracle noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi(x)=G(x,\zeta)-\mathbb E[G(x,\zeta)\mid x]\) be the centered oracle noise in a normed finite-dimensional space. It is conditionally \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian if, for every query \(x\), every dual vector \(u\), and every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), \[\mathbb E\!\left[\exp\!\left(\lambda\langle u,\xi(x)\rangle\right)\middle|x\right]\leq \exp\!\left(\frac{\lambda^2\sigma^2\|u\|_*^2}{2}\right).\] For an adaptive oracle, conditioning includes the complete pre-query history. This condition implies centeredness and Gaussian-type tails for every one-dimensional projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle noise is sub-Gaussian when every conditional directional projection has a Gaussian-dominated moment-generating function with a uniform scale parameter.
assumptions_latex: The centered noise \(\xi(x)\) is conditionally measurable and has finite directional moment-generating functions.
The inequality is required uniformly over query points and dual directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\exp(\lambda\langle u,\xi(x)\rangle)\mid x]\leq\exp(\lambda^2\sigma^2\|u\|_*^2/2)\) for all \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the leaf, but no source supports this exact conditional directional vector formulation. A source must also fix whether the test direction is in the primal or dual space and which norm, rather than leaving the pairing and dual-norm convention ambiguous.

children.title: Sub-Exponential Noise Regime
children.top_down_role: Complexity under intermediate tail concentration.

knowledge_statements.title: Sub-Exponential Noise Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional Bernstein moment-generating-function condition for directional stochastic-oracle noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi(x)\) denote centered oracle noise. It satisfies a conditional directional sub-exponential condition with parameters \((v,b)\) if, for every query \(x\), dual vector \(u\), and scalar \(\lambda\) satisfying \(|\lambda|<1/(b\|u\|_*)\), \[\mathbb E\!\left[\exp\!\left(\lambda\langle u,\xi(x)\rangle\right)\middle|x\right]\leq \exp\!\left(\frac{\lambda^2v^2\|u\|_*^2}{2}\right).\] Conditioning includes the pre-query history for adaptive algorithms. The restricted moment-generating-function domain permits tails heavier than sub-Gaussian tails while retaining exponential concentration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sub-exponential oracle noise obeys a quadratic moment-generating-function bound only near zero, producing Gaussian behavior for moderate deviations and exponential behavior for large deviations.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi(x)\) is conditionally centered for every query point.
Directional moment-generating functions exist whenever \(|\lambda|<1/(b\|u\|_*)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\exp(\lambda\langle u,\xi(x)\rangle)\mid x]\leq\exp(\lambda^2v^2\|u\|_*^2/2)\) on the stated interval.

notation.meaning: large-deviation scale limiting the mgf domain

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed near-zero MGF condition is a recognizable sub-exponential convention and the content kind fits, but sub-exponential parameterizations and admissible MGF domains vary. A specific authoritative locator is needed to support the exact (v,b) formula and norm convention.

children.title: Tail-Concentration Consequences
children.top_down_role: Effects of light-tail assumptions on probabilistic guarantees.

knowledge_statements.title: Tail-Concentration Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous high-probability bounds for predictable projections of concentrated oracle noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_m\) be conditionally centered oracle noises, and let \(u_t\) be pre-query measurable with \(\|u_t\|_*\leq1\). If every projection is conditionally \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian, then, for \(0<\delta<1\), \[\mathbb P\!\left(\max_{1\leq t\leq m}|\langle u_t,\xi_t\rangle|>\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2m/\delta)}\right)\leq\delta.\] Under the conditional sub-exponential condition \((v,b)\), the corresponding threshold is bounded, up to a universal constant, by \(v\sqrt{\log(2m/\delta)}+b\log(2m/\delta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sub-Gaussian and sub-exponential oracle assumptions convert into simultaneous high-probability bounds for any finite sequence of predictable directional noise projections.
assumptions_latex: Each \(u_t\) is measurable before the \(t\)-th oracle response and satisfies \(\|u_t\|_*\leq1\).
The noises satisfy the relevant conditional sub-Gaussian or sub-exponential condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{1\leq t\leq m}|\langle u_t,\xi_t\rangle|\) has order \(\sigma\sqrt{\log(m/\delta)}\) in the sub-Gaussian case and \(v\sqrt{\log(m/\delta)}+b\log(m/\delta)\) in the sub-exponential case.

notation.meaning: predictable dual direction at query t
number of oracle responses controlled simultaneously

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property belongs in Tail-Concentration Consequences, and the sub-Gaussian union-bound statement is mathematically plausible. The sub-exponential threshold, its constants, and its dependence on the selected (v,b) convention require a cited theorem or section.

children.title: Moment-Limited Noise Classes
children.top_down_role: Navigation for robust complexity under limited moment assumptions.

children.title: Heavy-Tailed Noise
children.top_down_role: Oracle noise lacking light-tail concentration.

knowledge_statements.title: Heavy-Tailed Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Heavy-tailed oracle noise in the absence-of-exponential-moments sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi(x)=G(x,\zeta)-\mathbb E[G(x,\zeta)\mid x]\). The oracle noise is heavy-tailed at \(x\) in the exponential-moment sense if it has a finite polynomial moment of some positive order but no positive exponential moment: \[\mathbb E[\|\xi(x)\|_*^p\mid x]<\infty\quad\text{for some }p>0,\qquad \mathbb E[\exp(\lambda\|\xi(x)\|_*)\mid x]=\infty\quad\text{for every }\lambda>0.\] A uniform heavy-tailed oracle class additionally specifies a common polynomial-moment bound over all admissible query points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Heavy-tailed oracle noise may possess finite polynomial moments while lacking every positive exponential moment, so sub-Gaussian and sub-exponential concentration do not apply.
assumptions_latex: The centered noise \(\xi(x)\) is defined whenever its conditional mean exists.
Heavy-tailed is interpreted specifically through failure of positive exponential moments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\xi(x)\) has some finite polynomial moment but satisfies \(\mathbb E[\exp(\lambda\|\xi(x)\|_*)\mid x]=\infty\) for all \(\lambda>0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record explicitly selects an absence-of-exponential-moments meaning, but heavy-tailed noise has multiple inequivalent definitions. An authoritative locator is required to justify this restrictive definition and its use as the intended noise class in this taxonomy.

children.title: Finite-Variance Robustness
children.top_down_role: Complexity achievable using variance alone.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Variance Robustness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: High-confidence mean recovery from finite-variance vector observations using robust aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_1,\\ldots,Y_m\) be independent vectors in a Hilbert space with mean \(g\) and \(\mathbb E\|Y_i-g\|^2\leq\sigma^2\). Partition the observations into \(k=\lceil 8\log(1/\delta)\rceil\) nonempty blocks, average within each block, and take a geometric median of the block means. When \(m\geq2k\), there is a universal constant \(C\) such that the resulting estimator \(\widehat g\) satisfies \[\mathbb P\!\left(\|\widehat g-g\|>C\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/\delta)}{m}}\right)\leq\delta.\] No exponential-tail assumption on the individual observations is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Median-of-means aggregation converts only a finite second moment into a sub-Gaussian-order high-confidence estimate of the mean, up to universal constants.
assumptions_latex: The vectors are independent with common mean \(g\).
\(\mathbb E\|Y_i-g\|^2\leq\sigma^2\) for every \(i\).
\(0<\delta<1\) and \(m\geq2\lceil8\log(1/\delta)\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widehat g-g\|\leq C\sigma\sqrt{\log(1/\delta)/m}\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The robustness property fits the leaf, but the dimension-free Hilbert-space geometric-median-of-means guarantee, nonidentical-observation formulation, block constants, and confidence range require a theorem-level source. The opening sequence also contains the malformed LaTeX text `Y_1,\\ldots,Y_m`, which must be repaired once the sourced theorem version is established.

children.title: Weak-Moment Regimes
children.top_down_role: Lower bounds under moments weaker than variance control.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Moment Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-noise class controlled by a moment of order strictly between one and two.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(p\in(1,2)\). A centered stochastic oracle belongs to the uniform weak-moment regime \((p,\sigma_p)\) if, for every admissible query \(x\), \[\mathbb E[\xi(x)\mid x]=0,\qquad \mathbb E[\|\xi(x)\|_*^p\mid x]\leq\sigma_p^p.\] For adaptive queries, both statements are conditional on the pre-query history. This class guarantees existence of the oracle mean but need not provide a finite variance or any exponential moment; consequently, procedures and rates requiring bounded second moments are not automatically applicable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weak-moment oracle has a uniformly bounded moment of order between one and two, ensuring a mean but allowing infinite variance and non-exponential tails.
assumptions_latex: The moment order satisfies \(1<p<2\).
The conditional mean of the oracle response exists at every admissible query.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\xi(x)\mid x]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[\|\xi(x)\|_*^p\mid x]\leq\sigma_p^p\) uniformly over queries.

notation.meaning: available moment order between one and two

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly isolates a p-th-moment regime with 1<p<2 and fits the terminal container. No cited source supports the exact uniform conditional oracle formulation or terminology, so an authoritative section or theorem locator is required.

children.title: Moment-Limited Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits arising when available moment control becomes insufficient.

knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Limited Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uniform mean recovery when no moment strictly above order one is controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m\) be independent real observations and let \(\widehat\mu_m\) be any estimator of their common mean. Over the class \(\mathcal P_1=\{P:\mathbb E_P|Y|\leq1\}\), no distribution-free error rate converging to zero exists uniformly: there is a universal \(c>0\) such that, for every \(m\), \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_1}\mathbb P_P\!\left(|\widehat\mu_m-\mathbb E_PY|\geq\frac14\right)\geq c.\] If only a moment of order \(p<1\) is assumed, the mean may not exist at all. Thus control of some moment strictly above one is the basic uniform mean-estimation boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded first absolute moment alone gives no uniform vanishing mean-estimation rate; below order one, the target mean itself may be undefined.
assumptions_latex: The estimator uses \(m\) independent observations.
The distribution class imposes only \(\mathbb E|Y|\leq1\), with no uniform integrability or higher-moment condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{\widehat\mu_m}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_1}\mathbb P_P(|\widehat\mu_m-\mathbb E_PY|\geq1/4)\geq c\), while a finite \(p\)-th moment for \(p<1\) does not ensure mean existence.

notation.meaning: distributions with first absolute moment at most one
arbitrary estimator based on m observations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is the correct mathematical role, and the qualitative distinction between first-moment-only classes and p>1 control is plausible. The stated uniform constant-probability lower bound at error 1/4 and the claim that this is the basic sharp boundary require a precise minimax impossibility source.

children.title: Geometry-Coupled Noise Classes
children.top_down_role: Navigation for noise coupled to the query point or local objective geometry.

children.title: State-Dependent Variance
children.top_down_role: Noise magnitude varying with the oracle query point.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Dependent Variance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional oracle variance bounded by a deterministic function of the query state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G(x,\zeta)\) be an unbiased stochastic gradient of a differentiable objective \(f\), and define \(\xi(x)=G(x,\zeta)-\nabla f(x)\). The oracle has state-dependent variance controlled by \(V:\mathcal X\to[0,\infty)\) if \[\mathbb E[\|\xi(x)\|_*^2\mid x]\leq V(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X.\] A common geometry-coupled specialization is \(V(x)=\sigma_0^2+\sigma_1^2\|\nabla f(x)\|_*^2\). Unlike a uniform bounded-variance model, the allowable noise level may grow or shrink as the query moves through the domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State-dependent variance allows the oracle's conditional noise level to vary with the query, often through the local gradient magnitude or another geometric quantity.
assumptions_latex: \(G(x,\zeta)\) is conditionally unbiased for \(\nabla f(x)\).
\(V(x)\) is finite at every admissible query point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\|G(x,\zeta)-\nabla f(x)\|_*^2\mid x]\leq V(x)\) for all \(x\in\mathcal X\).

children.title: Geometry-Coupled Noise
children.top_down_role: Noise controlled through local problem geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry-Coupled Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional second-moment noise measured in a local dual geometry and controlled by distance to the solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, let \(h\) induce the Bregman divergence \(D_h\), and let \(G(x,\xi)\) satisfy \(\mathbb E[G(x,\xi)\mid x]=\nabla f(x)\). The oracle has geometry-coupled noise relative to a solution \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin} f\) if constants \(\sigma_0,\sigma_1\ge 0\) exist such that
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[\|G(x,\xi)-\nabla f(x)\|_{x,*}^{2}\mid x\right]
\le \sigma_0^2+\sigma_1^2D_h(x^\star,x)
\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X.
\]
Here \(\|\cdot\|_{x,*}\) is the dual norm associated with the local geometry at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle variance is measured in the local dual norm and bounded by a constant plus a term proportional to geometric distance from a solution.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable on \(\mathcal X\).
\(h\) and the local norms are defined throughout \(\mathcal X\).
\(G\) is conditionally unbiased.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\|G(x,\xi)-\nabla f(x)\|_{x,*}^{2}\mid x]\le \sigma_0^2+\sigma_1^2D_h(x^\star,x)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical local-norm formulation of state- and geometry-dependent stochastic oracle variance
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but no cited source establishes this particular local-dual-norm variance model, the orientation of the Bregman term, or the relationship between h and the local norms. Those conventions materially determine the intended noise class.

children.title: Near-Solution Noise Behavior
children.top_down_role: Noise regimes distinguished by behavior close to target points.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Solution Noise Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies whether conditional oracle variance vanishes, persists, or diverges as queries approach the solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X^\star\subseteq\mathcal X\) be the solution set and define
\[
v(x)=\mathbb E\!\left[\|G(x,\xi)-\mathbb E[G(x,\xi)\mid x]\|_*^2\mid x\right].
\]
The noise is vanishing near solutions if \(v(x_k)\to0\) for every sequence \(x_k\) with \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,X^\star)\to0\). It is persistent if constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(X^\star\) satisfy \(c\le v(x)\le C\) for all \(x\in U\setminus X^\star\). It is locally unbounded if some such sequence satisfies \(v(x_k)\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a solution, conditional noise may vanish, remain uniformly positive and bounded, or become unbounded along an approaching sequence.
assumptions_latex: \(G(x,\xi)\) has a finite conditional second moment wherever \(v(x)\) is evaluated.
\(X^\star\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The limiting behavior of \(v(x)\) as \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^\star)\to0\) determines the vanishing, persistent, or locally unbounded class.

notation.meaning: conditional centered second moment of the oracle

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: limit-based classification of stochastic noise around a solution set
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The three behaviors are stated precisely and fit the condition container, but the record has no inspectable citation supporting these exact sequential and neighborhood-based definitions as the intended near-solution noise taxonomy.

children.title: Robustness-Identifiability Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Navigation for error floors, identifiability failures, and robustness limits.

children.title: Biased Oracle Error Floors
children.top_down_role: Accuracy limits imposed by persistent oracle bias.

knowledge_statements.title: Biased Oracle Error Floors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional strongly convex construction showing a nonvanishing optimization error under unknown bounded additive bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(\mu>0\) and \(\beta>0\). For \(s\in\{-\beta/\mu,\beta/\mu\}\), let \(f_s(x)=\frac{\mu}{2}(x-s)^2\) and let the deterministic oracle return
\[
G_s(x)=\nabla f_s(x)+\mu s=\mu x.
\]
Thus both objectives generate the same oracle transcript although their minimizers differ. For every possibly randomized output \(\widehat x\),
\[
\max_{s\in\{-\beta/\mu,\beta/\mu\}}
\mathbb E[f_s(\widehat x)-f_s(s)]\ge \frac{\beta^2}{2\mu}.
\]
Consequently, an unknown additive gradient bias bounded by \(\beta\) permits an error floor independent of the number of oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two strongly convex quadratics with different minimizers can produce identical biased gradients, forcing worst-case expected suboptimality at least β²/(2μ).
assumptions_latex: The algorithm observes only the displayed first-order oracle responses.
Additive oracle bias may be any constant with magnitude at most \(\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{\widehat x}\sup_s\mathbb E[f_s(\widehat x)-f_s(s)]\ge \beta^2/(2\mu)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The indistinguishable quadratic construction and constant beta^2/(2 mu) are mathematically consistent and the failure_boundary kind is appropriate. An authoritative source is nevertheless required for the exact biased-oracle model and lower-bound normalization.

children.title: Adversarial Contamination
children.top_down_role: Complexity under strategically corrupted observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Adversarial Contamination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional Huber contamination model for stochastic first-order oracle responses, allowing adaptive arbitrary corruptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_x\) be the clean conditional distribution of a first-order response at query \(x\). An \(\varepsilon\)-adversarially contaminated oracle returns a response with conditional law
\[
R_{x,H}=(1-\varepsilon)P_x+\varepsilon Q_{x,H},
\qquad 0\le\varepsilon<1,
\]
where \(H\) is the transcript before the response and \(Q_{x,H}\) is an arbitrary probability distribution chosen using \(x\) and \(H\). No moment, unbiasedness, or support condition is imposed on \(Q_{x,H}\) unless separately stated. The nonadaptive Huber model is recovered when \(Q_{x,H}=Q_x\) is independent of \(H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each oracle response is clean with weight 1−ε and otherwise drawn from an arbitrary, possibly transcript-adaptive contamination distribution.
assumptions_latex: \(P_x\) is a probability distribution for every admissible query \(x\).
\(Q_{x,H}\) is a probability distribution measurable with respect to the query and prior transcript.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{x,H}\in\{(1-\varepsilon)P_x+\varepsilon Q:Q\text{ is a probability distribution}\}\).

notation.meaning: clean response law at query x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conditional Huber contamination model specialized to adaptive first-order oracles
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but transcript-adaptive conditional contamination is stronger than the ordinary nonadaptive Huber model. No source is supplied for this exact adaptive convention or its measurability formulation.

children.title: Identifiability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where available information cannot distinguish target instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Identifiability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transcript-level overlap criterion under which no oracle algorithm can distinguish two optimization instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider instances \(i\in\{0,1\}\) with losses \(L_i(z)\) and admissible conditional oracle-law sets \(\mathcal R_i(x,H)\). If for every query-history pair \((x,H)\) reachable under a common transcript law there exists
\[
R_{x,H}\in\mathcal R_0(x,H)\cap\mathcal R_1(x,H),
\]
then an adversary can give every adaptive algorithm the same transcript distribution on both instances. Hence its output has a common law \(Q\), and its worst-case risk is at least
\[
\Delta=\inf_Q\max_{i\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{Z\sim Q}[L_i(Z)].
\]
If \(\Delta>0\), accuracy below \(\Delta\) is not identifiable from the oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If two instances admit the same response law after every reachable history, no adaptive method can distinguish them or guarantee risk below their separation radius.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm chooses each query measurably from its prior transcript and internal randomness.
The admissible response-law sets overlap along a common transcript process.
\(L_i\) is nonnegative and measurable for each instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_A\max_i\mathbb E[L_i(\widehat Z_A)]\ge\Delta\).

notation.meaning: admissible conditional response laws for instance i
common output distribution induced by indistinguishable transcripts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate and the separation-radius conclusion is plausible. The history-dependent overlap condition and its claimed implication for every adaptive algorithm require a source stating an equivalent transcript-coupling or oracle-indistinguishability result.

children.title: Robustness Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Corruption levels beyond which target guarantees cease to hold.

knowledge_statements.title: Robustness Breakdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Half-contamination threshold at which even a one-dimensional location, and therefore its optimizer, becomes unidentifiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(a>0\), and let the two clean laws be \(P_0=\delta_{-a}\) and \(P_1=\delta_a\). Under the Huber class
\[
\mathcal H_\varepsilon(P)=\{(1-\varepsilon)P+\varepsilon Q:Q\text{ is any probability law}\},
\]
if \(\varepsilon\ge\tfrac12\), the mixture \(R=\tfrac12\delta_{-a}+\tfrac12\delta_a\) belongs to both \(\mathcal H_\varepsilon(P_0)\) and \(\mathcal H_\varepsilon(P_1)\). Therefore any estimator \(\widehat s\) based on arbitrarily many observations from the contaminated oracle satisfies
\[
\max_{i\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_R[(\widehat s-s_i)^2]\ge a^2,
\qquad s_0=-a,\ s_1=a.
\]
Thus unrestricted contamination of at least one half destroys consistent identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At contamination one half or greater, two opposite point locations share a contaminated law, so their optimizer cannot be consistently estimated.
assumptions_latex: Contaminating distributions are unrestricted.
The contamination fraction satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge 1/2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{\widehat s}\max_i\mathbb E_R[(\widehat s-s_i)^2]\ge a^2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The shared-law construction is correct for every epsilon at least one half, and the squared-error constant a^2 follows from the two-point separation. The exact unrestricted-contamination breakdown claim still lacks an inspectable authoritative citation.

children.title: Stochastic Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Organizes distinctions that prevent direct comparison of stochastic complexity claims.

children.title: Probabilistic Success Regimes
children.top_down_role: Navigation for different probabilistic success requirements.

children.title: Expected-Error Regime
children.top_down_role: Stochastic complexity measured through expected output error.

knowledge_statements.title: Expected-Error Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle complexity measured by uniform expected suboptimality of the algorithm's prescribed output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an instance class \(\mathcal F\), algorithm \(A\), and output \(\widehat x_T\) after at most \(T\) oracle calls, define
\[
\mathcal E_T(A)=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f[f(\widehat x_T)-f_f^\star],
\qquad f_f^\star=\inf_{x}f(x).
\]
The expected-error complexity at accuracy \(\epsilon>0\) is
\[
T_{\mathrm{exp}}(\epsilon)=
\inf\{T\in\mathbb N:\exists A\text{ with }\mathcal E_T(A)\le\epsilon\}.
\]
The expectation includes oracle randomness and the algorithm's internal randomization; feasibility or stationarity losses may replace suboptimality only when explicitly specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected-error complexity is the fewest oracle calls needed for some algorithm to achieve worst-case expected suboptimality at most ε.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\) and the permitted oracle model are fixed.
\(f_f^\star\) is finite for every \(f\in\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}(\epsilon)=\inf\{T:\inf_A\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f[f(\widehat x_T)-f_f^\star]\le\epsilon\}\).

notation.meaning: algorithmic output after at most T oracle calls

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: minimax expected-risk definition of oracle complexity
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a coherent minimax expected-error complexity definition and its content kind matches the regime leaf. No source reference with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is attached.

children.title: High-Probability Regime
children.top_down_role: Stochastic complexity carrying an explicit failure probability.

knowledge_statements.title: High-Probability Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle complexity measured by a uniform tail guarantee at a prescribed failure probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an instance class \(\mathcal F\), accuracy \(\epsilon>0\), and failure probability \(\delta\in(0,1)\). For each \(f\in\mathcal F\), let \(f_f^\star=\inf_x f(x)\), and let \(\widehat x_T\) denote the output of an admissible algorithm after at most \(T\) oracle calls. The high-probability oracle complexity is
\[
T_{\mathrm{hp}}(\epsilon,\delta)=
\inf\!\left\{T\in\mathbb N:\exists A\text{ such that }
\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb P_f\!\left(f(\widehat x_T)-f_f^\star>\epsilon\right)\le\delta\right\}.
\]
Probability is taken jointly over oracle and algorithmic randomness. The same algorithm must satisfy the guarantee uniformly over \(\mathcal F\). If the displayed set is empty, \(T_{\mathrm{hp}}(\epsilon,\delta)=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: High-probability complexity is the smallest finite oracle-call budget, when one exists, for which one algorithm achieves suboptimality at most epsilon with probability at least 1 minus delta uniformly over the instance class.
assumptions_latex: \(\epsilon>0\) and \(\delta\in(0,1)\).
\(\mathcal F\) and the permitted oracle model are fixed.
\(f_f^\star=\inf_x f(x)\) is finite for every \(f\in\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(T_{\mathrm{hp}}(\epsilon,\delta)<\infty\), then an admissible algorithm using at most \(T_{\mathrm{hp}}(\epsilon,\delta)\) calls satisfies \(\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb P_f(f(\widehat x_T)-f_f^\star>\epsilon)\le\delta\).

notation.meaning: algorithmic output after at most T oracle calls

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: minimax tail-probability definition of oracle complexity

children.title: Confidence-Dependence Penalty
children.top_down_role: Additional complexity associated with stronger confidence requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Confidence-Dependence Penalty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares expected-error complexity with the oracle cost of a prescribed high-probability guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed instance and oracle classes, loss, and accuracy convention, let \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}(\epsilon)\) and \(T_{\mathrm{hp}}(\epsilon,\delta)\) denote the expected-error and high-probability complexities. When both quantities are finite, define the additive confidence comparison by
\[
\Pi_{+}(\epsilon,\delta)=T_{\mathrm{hp}}(\epsilon,\delta)-T_{\mathrm{exp}}(\epsilon).
\]
When additionally \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}(\epsilon)>0\), define the multiplicative comparison by
\[
\Pi_{\times}(\epsilon,\delta)=\frac{T_{\mathrm{hp}}(\epsilon,\delta)}{T_{\mathrm{exp}}(\epsilon)}.
\]
These quantities represent a nonnegative confidence penalty only under assumptions implying \(T_{\mathrm{hp}}(\epsilon,delta)\ge T_{\mathrm{exp}}(\epsilon)\). Any claimed dependence on \(\log(1/\delta)\) must identify which comparison is used and state the oracle-tail assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The confidence comparison is the finite additive difference or positive-denominator ratio between high-probability and expected-error complexities. It is a nonnegative penalty only when the chosen guarantee conventions imply that high-probability complexity is no smaller.
assumptions_latex: Expected-error and high-probability complexities use the same instance class, oracle model, loss, and accuracy convention.
\(\epsilon>0\) and \(\delta\in(0,1)\).
For \(\Pi_+\), both complexities are finite; for \(\Pi_\times\), also \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}(\epsilon)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pi_+(\epsilon,\delta)=T_{\mathrm{hp}}(\epsilon,\delta)-T_{\mathrm{exp}}(\epsilon)\) and \(\Pi_\times(\epsilon,\delta)=T_{\mathrm{hp}}(\epsilon,\delta)/T_{\mathrm{exp}}(\epsilon)\) on their stated domains.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit comparison of expected-risk and tail-risk oracle complexities

children.title: Stochastic Output Rules
children.top_down_role: Navigation for last-iterate, selected-iterate, and averaged-output criteria.

children.title: Last-Iterate Output
children.top_down_role: Guarantees evaluated at the final generated iterate.

knowledge_statements.title: Last-Iterate Output
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output convention returning the terminal point generated within the oracle-call budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let an iterative stochastic first-order method generate query points \(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_T\), where \(x_t\) is measurable with respect to the oracle transcript available before call \(t+1\). Under the last-iterate output rule, the reported point after \(T\) calls is
\[
\widehat x_T=x_T.
\]
Any complexity guarantee for this rule must evaluate its loss at \(x_T\) itself; a bound proved only for an average, a best iterate, or an independently selected iterate is not a last-iterate guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After T oracle calls, the method reports the terminal iterate x_T, and the stated loss guarantee must hold for that point.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm generates an indexed sequence \(x_0,\ldots,x_T\).
The oracle-call accounting convention identifies \(x_T\) as the terminal available iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x_T=x_T\).

notation.meaning: terminal iterate after the prescribed call budget

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The terminal-iterate convention is precise, uses the correct definition kind, and distinguishes it from averaging and iterate selection. It has no citation with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Selected-Iterate Output
children.top_down_role: Guarantees for an iterate chosen from the generated trajectory.

knowledge_statements.title: Selected-Iterate Output
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output convention choosing one generated iterate through a deterministic or randomized selection rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_0,\ldots,x_T\) be the iterates generated by a stochastic first-order method. A selected-iterate output has the form
\[
\widehat x_T=x_\tau,
\qquad \tau\in\{0,\ldots,T\},
\]
where \(\tau\) is chosen by a specified rule measurable with respect to the permitted transcript and auxiliary randomness. If \(\tau\) is independent of the iterates and \(\mathbb P(\tau=t)=p_t\), then for every nonnegative measurable loss \(L\), or every measurable \(L\) for which the displayed expectations are finite,
\[
\mathbb E[L(\widehat x_T)]=\sum_{t=0}^{T}p_t\,\mathbb E[L(x_t)].
\]
A best-iterate rule is admissible only when its selection statistic is observable under the stated oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The output is one generated iterate selected by a stated measurable rule. Under independent randomized selection, the expected value of any nonnegative or integrable loss is the probability-weighted average of the iterates' expected losses.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau\) takes values in \(\{0,\ldots,T\}\).
The selection rule uses only information allowed by the oracle model.
For the displayed identity, \(\tau\) is independent of the iterates and \(\mathbb P(\tau=t)=p_t\).
The loss \(L\) is nonnegative, or all displayed expectations are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x_T=x_\tau\), and under the stated independent-selection and integrability conditions, \(\mathbb E[L(\widehat x_T)]=\sum_{t=0}^{T}p_t\mathbb E[L(x_t)]\).

notation.meaning: performance loss evaluated at the output

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: randomized-iterate selection convention and total-expectation identity

children.title: Averaged Output
children.top_down_role: Guarantees evaluated on an aggregate of generated iterates.

knowledge_statements.title: Averaged Output
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output convention returning a convex combination of generated iterates, with weights fixed or transcript-measurable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_0,\ldots,x_T\) lie in a convex feasible set \(X\). Given nonnegative weights \(w_0,\ldots,w_T\) satisfying \(\sum_{t=0}^{T}w_t>0\), the averaged output is
\[
\widehat x_T=\frac{\sum_{t=0}^{T}w_t x_t}{\sum_{t=0}^{T}w_t}.
\]
Then \(\widehat x_T\in X\). If \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is convex and \(f^\star=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\) is finite, then
\[
f(\widehat x_T)-f^\star\le\frac{\sum_{t=0}^{T}w_t\bigl(f(x_t)-f^\star\bigr)}{\sum_{t=0}^{T}w_t}.
\]
For random weights, the denominator must be positive almost surely and the weighting rule must be admissible under the oracle filtration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The output is a nonnegative weighted average of iterates. It remains feasible, and for a convex objective with finite optimal value its error is bounded by the corresponding weighted average of iterate errors.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is convex and \(x_t\in X\) for every \(t\).
For the error inequality, \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is convex and \(f^\star=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)>-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x_T\in X\) and \(f(\widehat x_T)-f^\star\le(\sum_{t=0}^{T}w_t(f(x_t)-f^\star))/(\sum_{t=0}^{T}w_t)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convex-combination output rule and Jensen inequality

children.title: Output-Rule Separation
children.top_down_role: Lower-bound distinctions caused by the permitted output rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Output-Rule Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates stochastic guarantees according to the rule that converts an oracle transcript into the reported point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a measurable convex subset of a real vector space, let \(H_T\) be the transcript after \(T\) stochastic first-order queries, and let \(x_0,\ldots,x_T\in X\) be the generated iterates. An output rule is a measurable map \(O_T:H_T\mapsto X\). Last-iterate, selected-iterate, and averaged guarantees concern, respectively, \(O_T(H_T)=x_T\), \(O_T(H_T)=x_{I_T}\) for an \(H_T\)-measurable index \(I_T\in\{0,\ldots,T\}\), and \(O_T(H_T)=\sum_{t=0}^T w_{t,T}x_t\) for \(H_T\)-measurable weights satisfying \(w_{t,T}\geq0\) and \(\sum_{t=0}^T w_{t,T}=1\). A stochastic complexity guarantee must specify its output rule; validity for one output rule does not alone establish the same guarantee for another.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic guarantee is indexed by its measurable transcript-to-output map; last, selected, and averaged outputs are distinct unless an explicit comparison transfers the guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(T\in\mathbb{N}\).
\(X\) is a measurable convex subset of a real vector space and \(x_0,ldots,x_T\in X\).
Every reported output and every random index or weight used by the output rule is measurable with respect to \(H_T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For two output rules \(O_T^{(1)}\) and \(O_T^{(2)}\), a guarantee for \(O_T^{(1)}(H_T)\) does not, without an additional comparison, imply the corresponding guarantee for \(O_T^{(2)}(H_T)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: stochastic convergence statements depend on the specified measurable output rule

children.title: Horizon-Awareness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Navigation for horizon-aware and horizon-free stochastic guarantees.

children.title: Fixed-Horizon Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Stochastic guarantees tuned to a known query budget.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Horizon Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines guarantees for algorithms whose parameters may depend on a prescribed terminal query budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a query horizon \(T\in\mathbb{N}\). A stochastic first-order method has a fixed-horizon guarantee \(B(T,\delta)\) for error functional \(E\) if its initialization, step sizes, sampling rules, and output rule may depend on \(T\), and for every admissible problem instance \(P\),
\[\Pr_P\!\left(E_P(\widehat{x}_T)\leq B(T,\delta)\right)\geq1-\delta.\]
For an expectation guarantee, the displayed condition is replaced by \(\mathbb{E}_P[E_P(\widehat{x}_T)]\leq B(T)\). No claim is required at stopping times or deterministic times other than the prescribed \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-horizon guarantee holds at one prespecified budget, and the method and output rule may be tuned using that budget.
assumptions_latex: \(T\in\mathbb{N}\) is supplied before the method begins.
\(\delta\in(0,1)\) for a high-probability guarantee.
\(E_P(x)\geq0\) is the stated optimization error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{P}\Pr_P(E_P(\widehat{x}_T)>B(T,\delta))\leq\delta\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fixed-budget oracle guarantees permit horizon-dependent tuning
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent, distinguishes high-probability and expectation guarantees, and fits the fixed-horizon leaf. No inspectable source supports the stated convention that all listed method components may depend on the prescribed horizon.

children.title: Anytime Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Guarantees valid across stopping horizons without prior budget knowledge.

knowledge_statements.title: Anytime Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a single horizon-independent run whose guarantee holds simultaneously over all relevant query times.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A stochastic first-order method has an anytime guarantee \(B(t,\delta)\) for error functional \(E\) if its initialization and update policy do not require a terminal horizon and, for every admissible instance \(P\),
\[\Pr_P\!\left(\forall t\geq1:\ E_P(\widehat{x}_t)\leq B(t,\delta)\right)\geq1-\delta.\]
The same trajectory and confidence event cover all times. Consequently, for every almost surely finite stopping time \(\tau\) adapted to the oracle filtration, the event implies \(E_P(\widehat{x}_\tau)\leq B(\tau,\delta)\). A collection of separately tuned fixed-horizon runs is not an anytime guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An anytime bound uses one horizon-free run and one event that controls every time, hence also adapted finite stopping times.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat{x}_t\) is measurable with respect to the oracle history through time \(t\).
\(E_P(x)\geq0\) is the specified error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_P\Pr_P(\exists t\geq1:E_P(\widehat{x}_t)>B(t,\delta))\leq\delta\).

notation.meaning: Almost surely finite adapted stopping time.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: an anytime guarantee is a time-uniform statement for one horizon-independent process
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The time-uniform definition, single-trajectory requirement, and stopping-time consequence are internally consistent and fit the leaf, but no source with a specific locator is supplied for this comparatively strong simultaneous-event convention.

children.title: Horizon-Adaptation Cost
children.top_down_role: Complexity consequences of removing advance horizon knowledge.

knowledge_statements.title: Horizon-Adaptation Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the minimax penalty for restricting attention to one horizon-independent method class rather than methods tuned separately to each horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a problem class \(\mathcal{P}\), an oracle model, an output convention, and an expected-error functional \(E_P\). For each \(T\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{fix}}(T)\) be the class of admissible methods whose design may depend on \(T\), and let \(\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{any}}\) be a horizon-independent class whose members satisfy the designated simultaneous guarantee. Define \[R_{\mathrm{fix}}(T)=\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{fix}}(T)}\sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}}\mathbb{E}_{P,A}[E_P(\widehat{x}_T)]\] and \[R_{\mathrm{any}}(T)=\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{any}}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}}\mathbb{E}_{P,A}[E_P(\widehat{x}_T)].\] When every method in \(\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{any}}\) is also admissible in \(\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{fix}}(T)\), the additive horizon-adaptation cost is \(R_{\mathrm{any}}(T)-R_{\mathrm{fix}}(T)\). If \(R_{\mathrm{fix}}(T)>0\), the multiplicative cost is \(A(T)=R_{\mathrm{any}}(T)/R_{\mathrm{fix}}(T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Horizon-adaptation cost compares the minimax error of a nested horizon-independent method class with that of methods allowed to be tuned separately for the evaluation horizon.
assumptions_latex: \(T\in\mathbb{N}\).
Both risks use the same problem class, oracle model, output convention, and expected-error functional.
\(\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{any}}\subseteq\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{fix}}(T)\).
\(R_{\mathrm{fix}}(T)>0\) when the multiplicative cost is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{any}}(T)-R_{\mathrm{fix}}(T)\geq0\), and, when \(R_{\mathrm{fix}}(T)>0\), \(A(T)\geq1\).

notation.meaning: Class of methods allowed to depend on horizon T.
Anytime-class minimax expected risk evaluated at T.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: minimax risk is monotone under restriction of the admissible method class
exact literature convention may use ratios, additive gaps, or logarithmic overheads

children.title: Finite-Sum Access Models
children.top_down_role: Separates incremental lower bounds by the component information available to an algorithm.

children.title: Incremental First-Order Access
children.top_down_role: Navigation for indexed component values and gradients.

knowledge_statements.title: Incremental First-Order Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines component-indexed value and first-order queries for a finite-sum objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\) on a convex set \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\). An incremental first-order oracle accepts a query \((i,x)\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\times X\) and returns
\[\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{IFO}}(i,x)=(f_i(x),g_i(x)),\qquad g_i(x)\in\partial f_i(x).\]
When \(f_i\) is differentiable, \(g_i(x)=\nabla f_i(x)\). One oracle call reveals information about only the requested component; neither unqueried component values nor the aggregate gradient \(\nabla F(x)\) are returned unless the access model explicitly grants them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incremental first-order oracle returns the value and a gradient or subgradient of one requested finite-sum component at one point.
assumptions_latex: \(n,d\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is nonempty and convex.
\(f_i:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is proper and subdifferentiable at each queried point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{IFO}}(i,x)=(f_i(x),g_i(x))\) with \(g_i(x)\in\partial f_i(x)\).

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators
source_refs.locator: 5 Randomized coordinate update methods p. 113

children.title: Proximal Incremental Access
children.top_down_role: Navigation for componentwise gradient and proximal information.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Incremental Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines indexed access to a component value, a component subgradient, and a component proximal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\) on \(\mathbb{R}^d\), where each \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. A proximal incremental oracle accepts \((i,x,\lambda)\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\times\mathbb{R}^d\times(0,\infty)\), with \(x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f_i\) when first-order information at \(x\) is requested, and returns \[\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{PIO}}(i,x,\lambda)=\bigl(f_i(x),g_i(x),p_i\bigr),\qquad g_i(x)\in\partial f_i(x),\] where \[p_i=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f_i}(x)=\underset{z\in\mathbb{R}^d}{\operatorname{argmin}}\left\{f_i(z)+\frac{\|z-x\|^2}{2\lambda}\right\}.\] The response concerns only the requested component \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal incremental oracle returns the requested component's value and subgradient together with its proximal point at the supplied center and positive parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(n,d\in\mathbb{N}\).
For every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(\lambda>0\).
\(x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f_i\) when \(g_i(x)\) is requested.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The point \(p_i\) is uniquely defined and satisfies \((x-p_i)/\lambda\in\partial f_i(p_i)\).

notation.meaning: Returned component subgradient at the query point.

children.title: Hybrid Component-Aggregate Access
children.top_down_role: Navigation for models permitting occasional aggregate information.

children.title: Component-Only Query Phases
children.top_down_role: Finite-sum access restricted to individual components.

knowledge_statements.title: Component-Only Query Phases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines intervals of a hybrid finite-sum schedule containing component queries and no aggregate-information query.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a hybrid oracle schedule \((Q_t)_{t=1}^T\), where each \(Q_t\) is either a component query \(\mathsf{C}(i_t,x_t)\) or an aggregate-information query \(\mathsf{G}(x_t)\). A consecutive interval \(I=\{a,a+1,\ldots,b\}\subseteq\{1,\ldots,T\}\) is a component-only query phase if \[Q_t=\mathsf{C}(i_t,x_t)\quad\text{for every }t\in I.\] Thus no query of the declared aggregate-information type is issued during the phase. The endpoints may be deterministic or measurable with respect to the transcript available before the phase begins.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A component-only phase is a consecutive block of indexed component queries containing no query of the declared aggregate-information type.
assumptions_latex: \(T\in\mathbb{N}\).
Every query is classified as either \(\mathsf{C}(i_t,x_t)\) or \(\mathsf{G}(x_t)\).
\(1\leq a\leq b\leq T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathsf{G}}(I)=\sum_{t=a}^b\mathbf{1}\{Q_t=\mathsf{G}(x_t)\}=0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the record gives a formal schedule predicate for component-only access

children.title: Full-Gradient Queries
children.top_down_role: Access regimes permitting aggregate gradient information.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Gradient Queries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines aggregate gradient access for a differentiable finite-sum objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), where every component is differentiable on \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\). A full-gradient query at \(x\in X\) returns
\[\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{FG}}(x)=\nabla F(x)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\nabla f_i(x).\]
This response aggregates all components at the common point \(x\) and is therefore distinct from a single incremental query. In a hybrid complexity model, its cost must be stated either as one aggregate call or as a declared number, commonly \(n\), of component-query equivalents.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-gradient query returns the average of every component gradient at one common point, with its accounting cost explicitly declared.
assumptions_latex: \(n,d\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\).
\(f_i\) is differentiable at the queried point \(x\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{FG}}(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\nabla f_i(x)\).

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Gradient Information p. 27

children.title: Hybrid Access Schedules
children.top_down_role: Complexity models mixing component queries with aggregate queries.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Access Schedules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents adaptive interleavings of component and aggregate finite-sum oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A length-\(T\) hybrid access schedule is a sequence \(S_T=((A_t,Z_t))_{t=1}^T\), where \(A_t\in\{\mathsf{C},\mathsf{G}\}\) is the access type. If \(A_t=\mathsf{C}\), then \(Z_t=(i_t,x_t)\) specifies an indexed component query; if \(A_t=\mathsf{G}\), then \(Z_t=x_t\) specifies a full-gradient query. For an adaptive schedule, \((A_t,Z_t)\) is measurable with respect to the pre-query transcript and fresh internal randomness. Its resource vector is
\[(N_{\mathsf{C}},N_{\mathsf{G}})=\left(\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf{1}\{A_t=\mathsf{C}\},\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf{1}\{A_t=\mathsf{G}\}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid schedule records the adaptive order, locations, and counts of component and full-gradient queries.
assumptions_latex: \(T\in\mathbb{N}\).
Each query is issued before observing its own oracle response.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathsf{C}}+N_{\mathsf{G}}=T\).

notation.meaning: Index and point, or aggregate-query point.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: hybrid oracle algorithms are represented by typed, transcript-measurable query sequences
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the schedule leaf and the resource identity is correct. However, no source is supplied, and the phrase “pre-query transcript and fresh internal randomness” is not formalized by a filtration or conditional sampling convention.

children.title: Aggregate-Information Advantage
children.top_down_role: Rate changes enabled by occasional full-gradient information.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate-Information Advantage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares minimax risks with and without aggregate queries under a common component-query budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a problem class \(\mathcal{P}\), an error functional \(E_P\), and budgets \((q,r)\). Let \(R_{\mathrm{comp}}(q)\) be the minimax risk over algorithms using at most \(q\) component queries and no aggregate query. Let \(R_{\mathrm{hyb}}(q,r)\) be the minimax risk when at most \(r\) additional aggregate queries are allowed. Because the component-only algorithms form a subclass of the hybrid algorithms,
\[R_{\mathrm{hyb}}(q,r)\leq R_{\mathrm{comp}}(q).\]
The aggregate-information advantage is \(\Delta(q,r)=R_{\mathrm{comp}}(q)-R_{\mathrm{hyb}}(q,r)\geq0\); it is strict exactly when aggregate access lowers the optimal worst-case risk.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate-information advantage is the nonnegative minimax-risk reduction obtained by permitting aggregate queries in addition to the same component-query budget.
assumptions_latex: \(q,r\in\mathbb{N}_0\).
Both risks use the same problem class, error, randomization, and output conventions.
The hybrid model contains every component-only algorithm with budget \(q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta(q,r)=R_{\mathrm{comp}}(q)-R_{\mathrm{hyb}}(q,r)\geq0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: minimax risk is monotone under enlargement of the admissible algorithm class
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the leaf and follows from nesting of the algorithm classes, but the two minimax risks are described rather than formally defined, and no source supports this particular definition of aggregate-information advantage.

children.title: Index-Selection Policies
children.top_down_role: Navigation for prescribed, randomized, and adaptively selected component queries.

children.title: Oblivious Index Selection
children.top_down_role: Component choices fixed independently of observed oracle responses.

knowledge_statements.title: Oblivious Index Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines component-index schedules determined without using oracle responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_{t-1}\) be the oracle transcript before the \(t\)-th component query, and let \(U\) be an internal random seed sampled before oracle interaction and independently of the oracle's exogenous randomness. An index-selection policy is oblivious if there are measurable maps \(\phi_t\), fixed before oracle interaction, such that \[i_t=\phi_t(U)\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\quad\text{for every }t\geq1.\] Thus, conditional on \(U\), the entire index sequence is fixed and does not use component values, gradients, or other oracle responses in \(H_{t-1}\). Query points may still depend on the transcript unless the algorithm class separately imposes full obliviousness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An oblivious index policy determines its entire index sequence from a pre-sampled seed and fixed maps, without using observed oracle responses; its query points may still be adaptive.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb{N}\).
\(U\) is sampled before oracle interaction and independently of the oracle's exogenous randomness.
Each map \(\phi_t\) is fixed before oracle interaction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(t\geq1\), \(i_t=\phi_t(U)\), so the rule selecting \(i_t\) has no dependence on \(H_{t-1}\) beyond information already determined by \(U\).

notation.meaning: Component index queried at time t.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: an oblivious index sequence is fixed independently of observed oracle responses

children.title: Randomized Index Selection
children.top_down_role: Component choices driven by an internal random mechanism.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Index Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines randomized index choice through probability kernels, independently of whether the kernels are adaptive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_{t-1}\) be the transcript before component query \(t\). A randomized index-selection policy is specified by a measurable probability kernel \(p_t(\cdot\mid H_{t-1})\) on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) such that \[\Pr(i_t=j\mid H_{t-1})=p_t(j\mid H_{t-1})\quad\text{for every }j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}.\] The draw is generated using fresh internal randomness after \(H_{t-1}\) is available and before the response to query \(t\) is observed. The policy is nondegenerate at time \(t\) when the conditional distribution is not almost surely a point mass. History-independent kernels describe oblivious randomized sampling, whereas history-dependent kernels describe adaptive randomized sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomized index policy samples each component index from a declared conditional distribution after observing the available history but before receiving the current query response; the distribution may be fixed or adaptive.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb{N}\).
For every admissible history \(h\), \(p_t(\cdot\mid h)\) is a probability distribution on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
The kernel \(h\mapsto p_t(B\mid h)\) is measurable for every \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr(i_t=j\mid H_{t-1})=p_t(j\mid H_{t-1})\) for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

children.title: Adaptive Index Selection
children.top_down_role: Component choices responding to previously revealed information.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Index Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic or randomized adaptive policies in an indexed first-order oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), and let \(H_{t-1}=((i_s,x_s,Y_s))_{s<t}\) be the oracle transcript, where \(Y_s\) is the response to querying component \(i_s\) at \(x_s\). An index-selection policy is adaptive if, for every \(t\ge 1\), \(i_t\) is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(H_{t-1},U_t)\), where \(U_t\) is fresh internal randomness independent of the oracle instance. Thus the conditional law of \(i_t\) may depend on all previously queried indices, points, and oracle responses, but not on unobserved component information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adaptive policy chooses each component index using the complete observed query history and optional fresh randomness, without accessing unqueried component information.
assumptions_latex: \(F=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i\) is accessed through an indexed component oracle.
Internal random variables are independent of the unknown oracle instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i_t\text{ is }\sigma(H_{t-1},U_t)\text{-measurable for every }t\ge 1.\)

notation.meaning: Fresh internal randomness used at query t.

review_flags: Exact adaptive indexed-oracle convention requires a finite-sum lower-bound source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits Adaptive Index Selection, but the precise filtration, fresh-randomness, and unobserved-information convention requires a specific indexed finite-sum oracle source.

children.title: Index-Access Scope Separation
children.top_down_role: Lower-bound distinctions among progressively stronger selection rules.

knowledge_statements.title: Index-Access Scope Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates global transcript processing from component-local oracle access.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), an indexed-oracle algorithm satisfies index-access scope separation when its internal state and next pair \((i_t,x_t)\) may be arbitrary measurable functions of the past transcript and internal randomness, while the response at time \(t\) has the form \(Y_t=\mathcal O_{i_t}(f_{i_t},x_t)\). In particular, the query reveals no value, derivative, or side information about \(f_j\) for \(j\ne i_t\), except what is logically implied by the declared problem class and the previous transcript.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The algorithm may process its full history globally, but each oracle call reveals information only about the single selected component.
assumptions_latex: The finite sum is represented by indexed components \((f_i)_{i=1}^n\).
Oracle responses obey the declared component-oracle specification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y_t=\mathcal O_{i_t}(f_{i_t},x_t)\) contains no direct oracle information about any \(f_j\) with \(j\ne i_t\).

notation.meaning: Selected component and query point at time t.

children.title: Convex Finite-Sum Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Organizes finite-sum lower bounds by aggregate and component curvature.

children.title: Componentwise-Aggregate Convexity Regime

children.title: Componentwise Convexity
children.top_down_role: Finite-sum classes with convexity at every component.

knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity imposed separately on every finite-sum component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty convex subset of a real vector space and let \(f_i:C\to\mathbb R\) for \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). The finite-sum representation is componentwise convex on \(C\) if, for every index \(i\), all \(x,y\in C\), and every \(\theta\in[0,1]\), \[f_i(\theta x+(1-\theta)y)\le \theta f_i(x)+(1-\theta)f_i(y).\] This condition is representation-dependent: the same aggregate objective can admit one componentwise-convex decomposition and another decomposition containing nonconvex components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every component separately satisfies the convexity inequality on the common convex domain; the property depends on the chosen finite-sum decomposition.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty and convex.
Each \(f_i\) is real-valued on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_i\text{ is convex on }C\text{ for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}.\)

notation.meaning: Common convex domain of the components.
